1 PREAMBLE FOR AUTHORS

WarningI beg your attention please

This QMD script is a template/example. Among its characteristics :

  • A auto-foldable TOC is active (upper left panel)
  • Sections are numbered and anchored (example)
  • Source code is embedded (</> Code button in the upper-right corner)
  • The flatly CSS theme is applied
  • Lightbox available for images and plots
  • Width is filled with content to the right (up to 1600px by default)
  • The rendered HTML is self-contained (all dependencies/images are embedded in the HTML output)
  • Code chunks have a (context-dependent) background color and a blue (#31BAE9) left border
  • Chunk code lines are automatically numbered
  • Long code lines are automatically wrapped (this should not be actually in use due to the high grid:body-width value, but just in case you prefer deactivating it…).
  • Code annotation is active and is recommended. Same example
  • Callout collapsing is available and recommended to hide callouts corresponding to special cases : questions, and answers (roughly).
    • It is inactive by default (can be activated per-callout using collapse="true")
  • Code chunk output collapsing is available thanks to a knitr hook provided in the HTML header. It is useful in some cases (like, hiding a UMAP output for which an intuition question was asked), but please do not overuse it as it may make some trainees loose the track…
    • It is inactive by default (can be activated per-chunk using class.source="fold-hide")
  • An HTML code is provided in the HTML header to force the drawing of HTML tables border (only useful if one intend to use basic HTML tables rather than kable, by ex)? An example is provided here
  • A “hack” of callouts is used to color sections/chunks, depending on their purpose. See here.
  • In this template, R chunks always include the QMD #| label: and #| filename: with the same text value. This is a trick used to display the chunk name in the output, as a header for each evaluated chunk. This is useful to use as anchors to help trainees keep in synch between the projected output and the QMD source on their own screen. While using this trick is not mandatory, it is highly recommended.

2 Purpose of this session

Here is an example of a training session preamble : a very synthetic description of the upcoming content, with a specific warning from the very first training session (“Preproc.1”).
The targets of this section are the students.

This file describes the different steps to perform the first part of the single cell RNAseq data analysis training course for the EB3I n1 2026, covering these steps :

  • Load a single cell raw counts matrix
  • Remove barcodes from empty droplets
  • Estimate and remove ambient RNA contamination (“soup”)
ImportantAn important notice
  • These early (but mandatory) steps of the analysis are not covered by the renowned, higher-level analysis frameworks like Seurat nor scran/scater.
  • Thus, we will write/use a certain amount of lines of code, some of which of a higher complexity for R beginners.
  • Newcomer, do not fear !
    • While you are welcome to try writing some by yourself, depending on your R knowledge and self-confidence in it …
    • … you do not have to know how these code work …
    • … thus you should not feel ashamed copy-pasting the pre-written code hereafter …
    • … but in both cases, please try your best understanding what these code do, and even more, why !
    • In this purpose, you may use whatever help you can by searching.

4.1 Functions

4.1.1 SoupX helper function

This function was written to ease the use of SoupX on a Seurat object.
In practice, this code is already available in a separate script soupX_auto.R that will be sourced. It is just displayed here for educational purpose.
It was tested on SoupX = 1.6.2 with igraph = 1.5.1, Seurat = 4.4.0, 5.1.0

Code 
soupx_func
SoupX_auto <- function(scmat_filt = NULL,
                       scmat_raw = NULL,
                       soupQuantile = 0.9,
                       contaminationRange = c(.01, .8),
                       soupRange = c(0,100),
                       return_object = FALSE,
                       doPlot = FALSE) {
  
  ## Checks
  if(is.null(scmat_filt)) {
    stop('A filtered count matrix is required !')
  }
  
  if(is.null(scmat_raw)) {
    message('No unfiltered raw counts matrix provided. Estimation will be based on filtered matrix only.')
  }
  
  ## If no raw matrix
  if (is.null(scmat_raw)) {
    spChanRaw <- SoupX::SoupChannel(
      tod = scmat_filt,
      toc = scmat_filt,
      calcSoupProfile = FALSE)
    sc_rowsum <- sparseMatrixStats::rowSums2(scmat_filt)
    spProf <- data.frame(
      row.names = rownames(scmat_filt),
      est = sc_rowsum/sum(scmat_filt),
      counts = sc_rowsum)
    spChan <- SoupX::setSoupProfile(spChanRaw, spProf)
  } else {
    spChan <- SoupX::SoupChannel(
      tod = scmat_raw,
      toc = scmat_filt,
      calcSoupProfile = FALSE)
    if (min(spChan$nDropUMIs) > max(soupRange)) stop(
      'Minimum found counts per barcode is : ',
      min(spChan$nDropUMIs),
      ', which is smaller than the upper bound of soupRange !',
      ' Please increase soupRange max !')
    spChan <- SoupX::estimateSoup(sc = spChan,
                                  soupRange = soupRange)
  }
  ## Display Top 20 contributing genes
  if (!return_object) {
    cat('\nSoup-contributing features (Top 20) :\n')
    print(knitr::kable(head(
      spChan$soupProfile[order(spChan$soupProfile$est, 
                               decreasing = TRUE), ], 
      n = 20)))
  }
  ## Quick clustering needed
  spClust <- scran::quickCluster(scmat_filt, method = "igraph")
  ## Adding clusters to the SoupChannel object
  spChan <- SoupX::setClusters(sc = spChan, clusters = spClust)
  ## Estimating soup
  sX <- SoupX::autoEstCont(sc = spChan, 
                           doPlot = doPlot, 
                           tfidfMin = 1, 
                           soupQuantile = soupQuantile, 
                           maxMarkers = 100, 
                           contaminationRange = contaminationRange, 
                           rhoMaxFDR = .2, 
                           priorRho = .05, 
                           priorRhoStdDev = .1, 
                           forceAccept = FALSE)
  
  ## Removing soup (adjusting counts)
  if(return_object) {
    cat('Counts BEFORE SoupX : ', sum(scmat_filt), '\n')
    scmat_soupx <- SoupX::adjustCounts(
      sX, 
      method = 'subtraction', 
      roundToInt = TRUE, 
      tol = .001, 
      pCut = .01)
    cat('Counts AFTER SoupX : ', sum(scmat_soupx), '\n')
    rm(scmat_filt)
    return(scmat_soupx)
  } else return(sX$fit$rhoEst)
}
1
scmat_filt : (sparse)matrix corresponding to an empty droplets -filtered count matrix
2
scmat_raw : (sparse)matrix corresponding to an NON- empty droplets -filtered count matrix
3
soupQuantile, contaminationRange : see ?SoupX::autoEstCont
4
contaminationRange : range of the expected soup proportion
5
soupRange : estimate soup fraction from features with total reads comprised in this range of counts (only used when scmat_raw != NULL)
6
return_object : if TRUE, return the “unsouped” Seurat object ; if FALSE, only perform soup estimation and return the estimated proportion value (rho)
7
doPlot : Perform the SoupX estimation plot (rho distribution)
8
Check if a filtered matrix is provided
9
Check if an unfiltered matrix is provided
10
Handle the worst case of the unfiltered matrix not provided
11
Handle the better case of the unfiltered matrix provided

5 Data loading

Note

To ease the manipulation of input and intermediate/backups data (and mostly avoid losing time on trivial path problems), the students will just have to write their project code, and we will automatically build the expected in (data reading) and out (data writing) paths for them (as long as they don’t misspell their project code, which happens way more than I would like…).

Data should be retrieved and loaded from a Zenodo archive, and file identifiers will thus change in function of the training session block.

In case we may lose the internet connection to Zenodo (it happened in 2025 when CloudFlare went down!), a “local” backup is available on the IFB instance [NOTE : WILL be available : it has not yet been moved from the 2025 location for the moment, due to cluster being down and 2026 project id not yet defined and opened]

Warning

This section is a WIP : while the methods used in 2025 worked well (despite an early hiccup due to a typo from me), it was quite heavy to copy-paste and follow for students : all the code was written and readable in each RMD, which is not needed : this year everything will be thrown in a function loaded from an external (probably remote) script.

All parameters that may have to change depending on the situation (project code, local or remote, forcing dl or not, …) will become arguments of this function rather than variables, and the call should be a one-liner per retrieved/loaded file.

format:
  html:
    fig_width: 8
    fig_height: 6
    embed-fonts: true
    number-sections: true  ## Adds number to headers (sections)
    embed-resources: true  ## Make a self-contained HTML
    anchor-sections: true  ## Create HTML anchors for all section titles

      body-width: 1600px  ## Extends the main body to fill the right space up to 1600px
      margin-width: 0px
    smooth-scroll: true ## Smooth scroll of the HTML page
    code-fold: show  ## Show (unfold) code by default 
    code-tools:
      source: true  ## Show the upper-right "Code" button to allow downloading this source
      toggle: true
    code-block-bg: true  ## Use a (default grey) background for code chunks
    code-block-border-left: "#31BAE9"  ## Use a (here electric blue) left boarder for code chunks
    code-overflow: wrap  ## Wrap long code lines (should not be in use due to the high grid:body-width value, but just in case it is deactivated)
    code-line-numbers: true  ## Add line number to the left
    code-copy: true  ## Adds a button to copy chunk code to clipboard
    code-annotations: hover  ## For code annotation, show values in mouseover
    html-table-processing: none  ## Do not apply Quarto-specific rendering schemes for HTML tables
    echo: true
    fig-align: center
filters: 
 - foldablecodeblock.lua  ## LUA code for foldable code output

## Additional exercises / questions

-   Due to the heterogeneity of the trainees level or mood for R code, some may run the training course by their one, then feel bored. To keep them busy, we may sometimes have additional questions or exercises for them.
-   These are obviously not mandatory, and just a bit beyond the scope of our training courses.
-   These will appear as [**yellow**]{style="color:yellow;"} **callouts**.
-   Their solution will appear as [**orange**]{style="color:orange;"} **callout**
-   Both will be *collapsed* by default

::: {.callout-warning icon="false" collapse="true" style="background: yellow"}

# Example of code embedding and wrapping

> *Here is an example of a chunk containing a copy of a function (for display purpose) that is supposed to be sourced from this QMD script.*<br>Example of code chunk filenaming is provided.<br>Examples of code annotation are provided, to explain function parameters, and some condition testing.<br>*A small CSS hack was written to slightly move the "code-copy" button so that it does not interfere with the earliest annotations in the upper-right corner of the chunk*

## Functions

### SoupX helper function {#soupx-helper-function}

> This function was written to ease the use of SoupX on a Seurat object.<br>In practice, this code is already available in a separate script `soupX_auto.R` that will be **sourced**. It is just displayed here for educational purpose.<br>It was tested on `SoupX` = 1.6.2 with `igraph` = 1.5.1, `Seurat` = 4.4.0, 5.1.0

```{r}
#| label: soupx_func
#| filename: soupx_func
#| eval: false

SoupX_auto <- function(scmat_filt = NULL, # <1>
                       scmat_raw = NULL,  # <2>
                       soupQuantile = 0.9,  # <3>
                       contaminationRange = c(.01, .8),  # <4>
                       soupRange = c(0,100),  # <5>
                       return_object = FALSE,  # <6>
                       doPlot = FALSE) { # <7>
  
  ## Checks
  if(is.null(scmat_filt)) {
    stop('A filtered count matrix is required !') # <8>
  }
  
  if(is.null(scmat_raw)) {
    message('No unfiltered raw counts matrix provided. Estimation will be based on filtered matrix only.') # <9>
  }
  
  ## If no raw matrix
  if (is.null(scmat_raw)) { # <10>
    spChanRaw <- SoupX::SoupChannel( # <10>
      tod = scmat_filt,  # <10>
      toc = scmat_filt,  # <10>
      calcSoupProfile = FALSE) # <10>
    sc_rowsum <- sparseMatrixStats::rowSums2(scmat_filt) # <10>
    spProf <- data.frame( # <10>
      row.names = rownames(scmat_filt),  # <10>
      est = sc_rowsum/sum(scmat_filt),  # <10>
      counts = sc_rowsum) # <10>
    spChan <- SoupX::setSoupProfile(spChanRaw, spProf) # <10>
  } else { # <11>
    spChan <- SoupX::SoupChannel( # <11>
      tod = scmat_raw,  # <11>
      toc = scmat_filt,  # <11>
      calcSoupProfile = FALSE) # <11>
    if (min(spChan$nDropUMIs) > max(soupRange)) stop( # <11>
      'Minimum found counts per barcode is : ',  # <11>
      min(spChan$nDropUMIs),  # <11>
      ', which is smaller than the upper bound of soupRange !', # <11>
      ' Please increase soupRange max !') # <11>
    spChan <- SoupX::estimateSoup(sc = spChan,  # <11>
                                  soupRange = soupRange) # <11>
  } # <11>
  ## Display Top 20 contributing genes
  if (!return_object) {
    cat('\nSoup-contributing features (Top 20) :\n')
    print(knitr::kable(head(
      spChan$soupProfile[order(spChan$soupProfile$est, 
                               decreasing = TRUE), ], 
      n = 20)))
  }
  ## Quick clustering needed
  spClust <- scran::quickCluster(scmat_filt, method = "igraph")
  ## Adding clusters to the SoupChannel object
  spChan <- SoupX::setClusters(sc = spChan, clusters = spClust)
  ## Estimating soup
  sX <- SoupX::autoEstCont(sc = spChan, 
                           doPlot = doPlot, 
                           tfidfMin = 1, 
                           soupQuantile = soupQuantile, 
                           maxMarkers = 100, 
                           contaminationRange = contaminationRange, 
                           rhoMaxFDR = .2, 
                           priorRho = .05, 
                           priorRhoStdDev = .1, 
                           forceAccept = FALSE)
  
  ## Removing soup (adjusting counts)
  if(return_object) {
    cat('Counts BEFORE SoupX : ', sum(scmat_filt), '\n')
    scmat_soupx <- SoupX::adjustCounts(
      sX, 
      method = 'subtraction', 
      roundToInt = TRUE, 
      tol = .001, 
      pCut = .01)
    cat('Counts AFTER SoupX : ', sum(scmat_soupx), '\n')
    rm(scmat_filt)
    return(scmat_soupx)
  } else return(sX$fit$rhoEst)
}

```

1.  `scmat_filt` : (sparse)matrix corresponding to an empty droplets -filtered count matrix
2.  `scmat_raw` : (sparse)matrix corresponding to an NON- empty droplets -filtered count matrix
3.  `soupQuantile`, `contaminationRange` : see `?SoupX::autoEstCont`
4.  `contaminationRange` : range of the *expected* soup proportion
5.  `soupRange` : estimate soup fraction from features with total reads comprised in this range of counts (only used when `scmat_raw != NULL`)
6.  `return_object` : if `TRUE`, return the "unsouped" `Seurat` object ; if `FALSE`, only perform soup estimation and return the estimated proportion value (rho)
7.  `doPlot` : Perform the SoupX estimation plot (rho distribution)
8.  Check if a filtered matrix is provided
9.  Check if an unfiltered matrix is provided
10. Handle the worst case of the unfiltered matrix not provided
11. Handle the better case of the unfiltered matrix provided

# Data loading

::: {.callout-note}
To ease the manipulation of input and intermediate/backups data (and mostly avoid losing time on trivial path problems), the students will just have to write their project code, and we will automatically build the expected in (data reading) and out (data writing) paths for them (as long as they don't misspell their project code, which happens way more than I would like...).

Data should be retrieved and loaded from a Zenodo archive, and file identifiers will thus change in function of the training session block.

In case we may lose the internet connection to Zenodo (it happened in 2025 when CloudFlare went down!), a "local" backup is available on the IFB instance [**NOTE : WILL** be available : it has not yet been moved from the 2025 location for the moment, due to cluster being down and 2026 project id not yet defined and opened]

:::

::: {.callout-warning}
This section is a WIP : while the methods used in 2025 worked well (despite an early hiccup due to a typo from me), it was quite heavy to copy-paste and follow for students : all the code was written and readable in each RMD, which is not needed : this year everything will be thrown in a function loaded from an external (probably remote) script.

All parameters that may have to change depending on the situation (project code, local or remote, forcing dl or not, ...) will become arguments of this function rather than variables, and the call should be a one-liner per retrieved/loaded file.

:::
